rule: A post's optional written_by names the firefly that wrote it for whoever signs it, as the writer's client reports it: an object with agent, an agent:<id> address with no whitespace and at most 200 characters after agent:, and name, nonempty after trimming, at most 120 code points, with no control, format or line-break character. Both are trimmed; other keys are ignored. Any other value drops the field with warning invalid_written_by and the post stays valid. It is a claim, like author: it grants, refuses and ranks nothing, and a reader never resolves it.
writer_rule: Who wrote a post, for the question who did this: the firefly its written_by names when it names one (written_by.agent), else its author (a legacy actor_ref when it has no author), else nobody. Two posts have the same writer exactly when that string is equal. So a firefly's post is the firefly's and never its person's, two fireflies writing for one person are two writers, and a written_by dropped as malformed names no firefly. Marks fold by writer: one writer's repeat of a mark value on a target counts once, and a mark whose writer is nobody stays distinct by id. The person stays in author. On a hosted service the signer the service set from the sign-in stands where author stands here. A reading over two claims: it resolves nothing and grants nothing.
expected_fields: parse_post: status, written_by (null when absent or dropped), warnings (field and warning). post_writers: writers, each post id with its writer or null for nobody. reconstruct_timeline: target, and marks, the marks folded onto it in fold order, each with id, mark, author (as written, an empty string when absent) and writer (null for nobody).
